about: Well-known places of the sky, the most cited first. Each has a name to show, its other names, a kind in plain words, and ra and dec in degrees (ICRS): where the object is at `epoch`, a star with a measured proper motion having been moved there from its position of 2000. A `fast` star, one that moves more than half an arcsec a year, also carries its catalogue astrometry: position and epoch, proper motion in mas a year (pmra is the motion in right ascension times cos(dec)), parallax in mas, radial velocity in km/s or null. A star brighter than magnitude 5 in the V band also carries `vmag`. `letters` and `constellations` say how the designations of stars are spelled: the abbreviations SIMBAD uses, and the words written here.
source: SIMBAD astronomical database, CDS, Strasbourg (Wenger et al. 2000, A&AS 143, 9), tables basic and ident, read through its TAP service. This research has made use of the SIMBAD database, operated at CDS, Strasbourg, France.

selection: The Messier objects; stars with a common name and a Bayer, Flamsteed or Bright Star number; other objects with a common name that at least 50 papers cite (20 for one with an NGC or IC number, 500 for one whose common names are all abbreviations); stars and brown dwarfs with a parallax of at least 150 mas; variable stars that at least 500 papers cite.
